constraints.text: Lab-grown stones and the US tariff. Industry estimates put lab-grown at about a quarter of the US diamond jewellery market; Botswana's finance ministry warned that 15% US tariffs, with possible Indian duties, could prolong the slump. The 37% rate of an earlier proposal is not the final one.

paradoxes.text: Gaborone presses De Beers to sell more and to hand over a larger stake, yet it holds 12 million carats, nearly double its own ceiling. The market, not the stake, is the binding limit: a bigger stake makes the state co-owner of stones it cannot sell.

grand_strategy.reading: Botswana's grand strategy is to turn diamond dependence into state control: a bigger stake in De Beers, a say over sales, and a budget that survives the slump, with Debswana carrying about 90% of national diamond sales. The lab-grown glut and the US tariff erode the value of that stake faster than negotiation can raise it, so Gaborone is reported to be settling for about 25% rather than the majority it wanted. South Africa is the partner it leans on (SACU, the rand, the ports); Namibia, Zimbabwe, the EU and the UK are not yet read from sources, and the card is thinner than its tier because the call budget ran out.

stances.note: South Africa is the customs-union partner and the rand neighbour. The state visit of 20-21 May 2026 and the Bi-National Commission, the first since 2022, show warming (official source). The rand matters: the pula lost about 7.2% against it in the year to August 2026 (Bank of Botswana). Bond none: no source names kinship or affinity, and the tie is SACU and trade. Partner is our reading of a customs union with no defence clause, and it is the Pretoria side's own official voice, not a grade a source gives.

Partner: SACU and rand neighbour, no defence clause. The Presidency announced the state visit of 20-21 May 2026 and the sixth Bi-National Commission (the last was in 2022), the first at this level in four years: warming. Botswana is also a large buyer (exports of about USD 4.38bn in 2025, led by fuels, per UN Comtrade as shown on Trading Economics, tier 4), and the pula lost about 7.2% against the rand in the year to August 2026 (Bank of Botswana): Pretoria holds the currency and the ports Gaborone depends on.
